candidates.name: C1 — SANCTION: Default-Deny Occupancy with Conformally Calibrated Semantic Exemptions
candidates.core_idea: Invert the identification problem: RGB-D occupancy is keep-out BY DEFAULT, and the semantic layer's only job is to SANCTION exemptions (target, destination, support surface, grasp corridor). Identification errors then delete exemptions and fail SAFE (liveness cost), never delete keep-outs (safety cost).
candidates.mechanism: Per episode, and re-grounded at chunk boundaries: (1) Depth from agentview + eye-in-hand (calibration constants and two-view funnel already validated in v18) builds a voxel occupancy / SDF over the workspace above the table plane; robot links and the currently-grasped payload are masked out via FK (link checkpoints already exist). (2) Occupancy is inflated by a conformal quantile calibrated PwC-style on the 400 saved episodes where GT object positions are known — the inflation absorbs our measured 8–13cm grounding error with a coverage guarantee instead of hand-tuned radii. (3) The exemption set is proposed semantically: symbolic MENTIONED parsing (validated, 100% component of the v17 rule) names target and destination; open-vocab detection grounds them to 3D regions; the validated ON_TOP_OF/SUPPORTS predicate exempts the support under target/destination; the grasp corridor is an anisotropic cone from EEF to the sanctioned target (the exact 'semantic target-corridor exemption' already flagged as the next lever for the L1 frontier, and the P0 steering-stack cone item). (4) An exemption is GRANTED only when independent evidence agrees — detector grounding, VLM N-sample majority on a crop ('is this the task target?', name-then-match style), and optionally the policy-attention peak (Park et al. as one oracle inside our sanctioning logic, not the whole mechanism). Agreement frequency is the nonconformity score, conformalized ConU-style as conformal RISK control: bound the exemption false-positive rate at alpha, let liveness float. (5) Withheld/uncertain exemption degrades to conservative mode (velocity cap + intact keep-out) rather than task abort. Non-exempt occupied space compiles to the keep-out SDF the validated in-denoising DCBF guidance already consumes; guidance (unlike our dead post-hoc shield) lets the policy re-plan around the denied space, which is what makes default-deny survivable for TSR.
candidates.hazard_coverage: Geometric: complete, including UNNAMED and DYNAMIC hazards (a human hand or an object the VLM never detects is occupied, hence keep-out — no other candidate covers hazards nobody identified). Property/relational: only indirectly (occupied regions can inherit inflated margins from property votes, but that is C2 machinery). Instruction-level: only the degenerate case (ungroundable/contradictory target -> empty exemption set -> refuse). Damage/force: partial via conservative-mode velocity caps.
candidates.novelty_vs_survey: Both surveys independently name this white-space #1: 'nobody does default-deny with semantic exemption' and 'calibrated EXEMPTION gating does not exist — nobody calibrates the decision to REMOVE protection'. Nearest neighbors to cite and beat: Park et al. 2606.09749 (object-level default-deny with a single uncalibrated attention-derived exemption; breaks on place tasks needing destination exemptions) and OGM-CBF 2405.10703 (occupancy keep-out, zero exemptions, navigation). Delta: occupancy-level formulation, multi-source semantic sanction (target+destination+support+corridor), conformal risk control on exemption FPR, and the fail-safe error-direction argument, which is absent from every surveyed paper. Defensible: yes, provided Park and OGM-CBF are cited explicitly and attention is subsumed as one exemption oracle.
candidates.compilation_to_constraints: Non-exempt occupancy -> keep-out SDF/superquadric union (native input to our DCBF guidance); conformal inflation -> margins; withheld exemption -> velocity box (conservative mode); exempt corridor -> anisotropic cone carve-out (already a P0 steering item); empty/ambiguous exemption set -> router REFUSE; destination-sanction failure with valid target -> router REDIRECT (place on nearest sanctioned support). Rotation locks: not native — supplied by C2 if composed.
candidates.failure_safety: Fail-safe BY CONSTRUCTION for geometry: a missed hazard is impossible because hazards are never enumerated — everything is a hazard until exempted. The ONLY unsafe error is a false exemption, which is precisely the conformally bounded quantity. Wrong identification -> withheld exemption -> slower/failed task, CAR unaffected. This is the cleanest fail-safe story of the four and the paper's most quotable claim.
candidates.cost_weeks: 3-4 weeks: occupancy+FK masking ~1 (depth, calibration, and link checkpoints all exist); exemption/sanction logic ~1 (MENTIONED, SUPPORTS, corridor carve-out largely exist); conformal calibration on saved episodes ~0.5-1; guidance integration + smokes ~1. Cheap iteration: E2 corridor precompute predicts TSR ceiling offline before any rollout.
candidates.risks: (1) Corridor/liveness — the exact failure that killed v18 pixels-only TSR (34.5 vs 40 baseline); mitigations: in-denoising enforcement re-plans (Tier-GT proof: 86.5 TSR at L2), explicit corridor exemption, and the E2 offline gate before GPU commit. (2) Depth-only occupancy artifacts (shadows, table-plane bleed) inflating denied space. (3) Calibration set (~400 episodes, 4 tasks) may be too homogeneous for meaningful 1-alpha. (4) SafeLIBERO's sparse scenes understate clutter stress; multi-object scenes in LIBERO-Safety are the real test.
candidates.benchmark_fit: SafeLIBERO: headline (identification-swap vs AEGIS's single-VLM-pick, attacking its admitted bottleneck). LIBERO-Safety TSA/FSHOA: strongest fit of any candidate — the intruding human hand is never task-mentioned, so default-deny covers it with zero extra machinery (first method rows). OopsieVerse: partial (approach-impact damage via conservative mode; grip crush honestly out of scope). SSR: only the degenerate refuse case.

candidates.name: C2 — FOL-COMPILE v2: Neuro-Symbolic Hazard Compiler with Conformalized Predicates and Runtime Rule Authorship
candidates.core_idea: Generalize the validated 100%-vs-0-10% decomposition to all five hazard classes: the VLM performs only LOCAL, individually verifiable micro-judgments (name this crop, attribute one property, verify one relation), while ALL scene-level hazard decisions are FOL over grounded predicates; each rule carries a compilation head naming the constraint class it emits, and per-predicate vote frequencies are conformalized so uncertain predicates enforce the worst-case constraint in their conformal set.
candidates.mechanism: Three layers, most already built. (1) Predicate grounding: existing validated predicates (MENTIONED via name-then-match, SUPPORTS/ON_TOP_OF, NEAREST_TO_PATH, HOLDING) extended with relational-state predicates from RGB-D geometry (ON(x,y), ABOVE(x,y), NEAR_EDGE(x, table), INSIDE) and property predicates from N=5 multi-prompt majority voting (IS_HOT, IS_FRAGILE, IS_SPILLABLE, IS_SHARP, IS_LIQUID_CONTAINER) — asset (b), plus the 2512.08233 ChatGPT pairwise-risk recipe as an offline prior table for severity. (2) Rule layer: the validated OBSTACLE(x) := NOT-MENTIONED AND NOT-SUPPORTS AND NEAREST-TO-PATH rule; a template library for relational hazards (ABOVE(held_liquid, electronics) -> rotation_lock + keep-out-above; ON(flammable, stove_lit) -> keep-out + refuse-to-place; NEAR_EDGE(x) -> margin + slow); and runtime VLM rule authorship via Prompt D (built and verified in v16: VLM composes new rules like HOLDING(eef,mug) AND NEAR(eef,laptop) -> slow + rotation_lock from the grounded vocabulary only — it cannot invent ungroundable predicates, which is what makes authored rules executable). Instruction-tier rules take the parsed task predicate itself as antecedent (TASK_TARGETS(fragile_x, strike) -> REFUSE; destination unsafe -> REDIRECT), giving an SSR answer grounded in physical predicates — exactly the 'explicit reasoning simulating physical properties' LIBERO-Safety prescribes for the unsolved L2 tier. (3) Calibration: per-predicate sampling-consistency frequencies conformalized ConU-style on an extended offline benchmark (~150-200 labeled scenes from the 400 saved episodes); a predicate whose conformal set contains both values triggers the UNION of implied constraints — 'enforce the conformal hull', the first identification-to-enforcement guarantee.
candidates.hazard_coverage: Broadest of all candidates: geometric (validated rule), property (votes -> margins/velocity caps/rotation locks), relational-state (ON/ABOVE/NEAR_EDGE templates — the towel-on-stove class), instruction-level (task-predicate rules -> refuse/redirect), damage/force partially (caution class-K + velocity boxes; grip crush honestly excluded). The only candidate covering the full taxonomy in one formalism.
candidates.novelty_vs_survey: Three named white-spaces at once: runtime rule authorship (RoboGuard grounds PRE-DEFINED rules; Safety Chip/SafeManip use human-authored specs — 'a VLM writing new FOL rules per scene from a grounded predicate vocabulary has no direct precedent'); first CALIBRATED semantic-hazard identifier (survey-2 gap #3: 'no paper gives guarantees for property attribution or relational-state hazards'); heterogeneous compilation contract + router (survey-1 gap #2: 'nobody unifies them behind one identification stack'). Closest threat: CORE 2602.19983 — differentiate on manipulation predicates, constraint heterogeneity beyond keep-out, conformal (not martingale) guarantees, and our published-strength ablation (VLM whole-scene 0-10% vs symbolic 100% on identical data). Defensible, with CORE and SafetyDetect cited.
candidates.compilation_to_constraints: The compilation head IS the design: every rule template and every authored rule declares its emission — keep-out superquadric/ellipsoid (validated geometry), margin (property severity), velocity box (caution class-K, precedent: Brunke 0.25h^2 and 2603.21142, done per-constraint not globally), rotation lock (spillable/liquid transport), REFUSE/REDIRECT (instruction-tier rules to the router). Conformal-hull enforcement: uncertain predicate -> union of implied constraints, worst case enforced.
candidates.failure_safety: NOT inherently fail-safe — a missed rule or false-negative predicate is a missing constraint (fails unsafe), the same error direction as Brunke/AEGIS/CORE. Mitigations that partially repair this: conformal-hull worst-case enforcement (uncertainty fails toward MORE constraint), abstention -> conservative class (slow mode), and composability with C1 as a geometric floor beneath it. Report the residual honestly: the fail-safe claim belongs to C1; C2's claim is coverage + calibration.
candidates.cost_weeks: 2-3 weeks — the cheapest headline-capable option because most code exists: v17 grounder, v16 Prompt D injection (bug-fixed, verified), property priors, superquadric compiler, router hooks. New work: relational predicates from RGB-D (~0.5), template library (~0.5), ConU calibration + extended labeled benchmark (~1), SSR offline eval (~0.5).
candidates.risks: (1) Predicate grounding fidelity is the fragile link (SafetyDetect's 96%->82.7% sim-to-real drop; our own 0.22m median grounding error at runtime) — relational predicates inherit it. (2) Rule-authorship quality with locally servable VLMs: 3B/7B failed whole-scene reasoning; Prompt D worked but its rules were TSR-neutral on Spatial — value must be demonstrated on property/relational suites, not assumed. (3) Coverage illusion: template library can be gamed as 'hand-written rules' by reviewers — the authored-rule ablation must carry that argument. (4) CORE proximity requires careful writing.
candidates.benchmark_fit: SafeLIBERO: identification-swap headline plus the semantic constraint classes SOTA 2607.01378 cannot express. LIBERO-Safety SSR: the L2 contextual-trap tier (published best 20-36% refusal) is the marquee target — predicate-grounded instruction rules are precisely the prescribed fix; TSA/FSHOA via caution/velocity classes. OopsieVerse RoboCasa: property->caution compilation is the natural first method row (impact damage only).

candidates.name: C3 — GRAD-RISK: Task-Conditioned Analytic Risk Field for Graded In-Denoising Guidance
candidates.core_idea: Replace binary hazard/safe calls with a continuous risk potential: every detected object contributes a graded field conditioned on (held object, object properties, task phase), consumed natively by the denoising loop as a repulsor energy plus per-region class-K modulation — identification becomes soft weighting rather than discrete selection.
candidates.mechanism: Zero-training and analytic, to fit the runway: risk(x) = sum_i severity_i * compat(held, obj_i) * kernel(||x - c_i||; extent_i). Severity_i comes from our N=5 property vote frequencies (asset b) mapped through a severity table; compat(held, obj_i) is a pairwise interaction prior (water-above-laptop high, bowl-near-plate low) generated OFFLINE once via the 2512.08233 ChatGPT pairwise-rating recipe over the ~40 object categories appearing in our three benchmarks — a one-day, one-time LLM cost; kernel/extents from RGB-D detection with the v18 funnel. Task-phase conditioning: the field is re-weighted by HOLDING state (empty gripper vs carrying liquid vs carrying rigid), which our FOL predicates already track at runtime — this is what no static risk map has. Consumption is where it becomes ours: (1) as a soft hinge-gradient pre-shaping term on the x1-prediction rollout inside denoising (P0 steering item 4 — analytic gradient, zero extra NFEs), graded by risk instead of binary barrier membership; (2) as per-region class-K aggressiveness: alpha_i(h) = (1 - risk_i)*h^2 scaling smoothly between nominal and Brunke-style caution; (3) a conformal lower bound on the field (Conformalized Distance Fields machinery) turns the soft field into calibrated hard margins where risk exceeds a threshold, giving a principled soft-to-hard escalation matching our select->guide->project->certify principle.
candidates.hazard_coverage: Property hazards (hot/fragile/sharp -> graded standoff) and pairwise relational hazards (spill-sensitive pairs) as continuous margins and velocity modulation. Geometric only through detections (misses undetected objects). NO instruction tier, NO discrete constraint types (rotation locks need a side-channel), no relational-STATE hazards (towel already on stove is a state, not a distance).
candidates.novelty_vs_survey: Weakest of the four and must be said plainly: 2512.08233 owns dense manipulated-object-conditioned risk fields (with 100% human-alignment results); Language-as-Cost owns anticipatory semantic costmaps; OmniGuide owns VLM energy guidance in pi0.5 denoising. Our residual delta — zero-training analytic composition from vote frequencies, HOLDING/phase conditioning at runtime, in-denoising graded consumption, conformal field bound — is a systems combination, not a new identification principle. Defensible only as a supporting mechanism inside C2's margin/velocity classes, not as a headline.
candidates.compilation_to_constraints: Margins (conformal field threshold -> inflated keep-out), velocity boxes (risk-scaled class-K / v_max), attractor-repulsor guidance energy (native to our loop). Rotation locks and router decisions: NOT expressible — requires C2/C4 alongside. This partial compilation is exactly the survey's criticism of the risk-field family; adopting it alone would inherit that criticism.
candidates.failure_safety: Fails UNSAFE when risk is underestimated (miscalibrated severity, missed detection, wrong compat prior) — same direction as all continuous-field prior work. The conformal lower bound repairs calibration error but not detection misses. No inversion trick available: a field built from detected objects cannot be default-deny.
candidates.cost_weeks: ~1.5-2 weeks (severity table + compat prior 0.5, field + guidance term 0.5 since hinge pre-shaping is already a P0 item, conformal bound + eval 1) — but it competes for the same guidance-integration slot as C1/C2 rather than adding coverage.
candidates.risks: (1) Novelty attack from 2512.08233 is the dominant risk — a reviewer can call this 'their field, our consumer'. (2) Graded repulsion inside denoising can reintroduce the SafeDiffuser-RoS always-push pathology our steering research explicitly blacklisted for uniform application. (3) Severity/compat tables are uncalibrated common sense unless the conformal bound genuinely binds. (4) Adds a continuous tuning surface (kernel widths) that burned weeks in v18/v19 barrier-shaping with zero net TSR.
candidates.benchmark_fit: OopsieVerse RoboCasa is its best fit (graded damage-avoidance margins near fragile assets, phase-conditioned caution while carrying); SafeLIBERO only as an ablation flavor of margins; contributes nothing to LIBERO-Safety SSR.

candidates.name: C4 — GOVERNOR: Root-of-Trust Scene Judge with Response-Modality Router
candidates.core_idea: A guardrail-centric top tier: an instruction-channel-isolated VLM governor consumes the grounded predicate state (not raw pixels, not the raw user instruction) and ROUTES each hazard to the right response modality — refuse / redirect / constrain(class) / modulate — making the routing decision itself, currently absent from every surveyed system, the contribution.
candidates.mechanism: Architecture lifted from RoboGuard's root-of-trust lesson and upgraded from plan-veto to constraint emission. (1) Isolation: the governor is prompted with the scene's grounded predicate state (C2's predicate layer as its world model: object names, properties from votes, relations from RGB-D) and a paraphrased task intent — never the verbatim user instruction — so instruction-level attacks and L2 contextual traps are judged against physical state, not persuasive text. (2) Judgment: for the task as a whole and for each hazard hypothesis, the governor emits a tuple (hazard, modality, constraint_class, params): e.g., ('strike mug with hammer', REFUSE, -, -), ('place cup on laptop', REDIRECT, destination:=table_free_region, -), ('towel near lit stove', CONSTRAIN, keep-out+margin, obj=stove), ('carrying knife', MODULATE, velocity_box+rotation_lock, v_max=0.08). N-sample majority over tuples; modality decisions conformalized on an offline labeled set (LIBERO-Safety SSR pairs + our extended scenes), with the KnowNo-lineage machinery but the abstention target replaced by an autonomous conservative default (deny/slow persists; no human oracle) — the act-vs-conservative-default policy the calibration survey flags as essentially unstudied. (3) Execution: REFUSE/REDIRECT go to the episode router; CONSTRAIN/MODULATE tuples compile through the existing constraint classes into DCBF guidance. The governor runs once per episode plus on re-ground triggers (grasp events, stall detection), so latency is off the control path.
candidates.hazard_coverage: Instruction-level hazards are the core competence (L0 explicit, L1 commonsense, L2 contextual traps — judged on grounded physical predicates, the exact mitigation LIBERO-Safety prescribes). Relational-state hazards via predicate input. Property hazards routed to modulation. Geometric hazards NOT its job (delegated downward); damage/force only as modulation. As a standalone it is a refusal system with extras; its coverage argument requires C1/C2 beneath it.
candidates.novelty_vs_survey: Survey-1 names the gap verbatim: 'no published system routes a hazard to the right response modality (refuse vs redirect vs constrain vs modulate)' and calls RoboGuard-governor + continuous CBF-class constraints in one stack 'untaken white space'. Deltas vs RoboGuard: rules scene-discovered (via C2) not pre-defined; output is continuous constraint classes not LTL plan vetoes; conformal modality gating with autonomous fallback vs architectural trust alone. Vs SOL: minimal-deviation constraint emission vs binary action gating. Vs KnowNo/IntroPlan lineage: no human in the loop. Defensible as a tier; thin as a whole paper.
candidates.compilation_to_constraints: Router decisions are the NATIVE output (refuse/redirect first-class); CONSTRAIN/MODULATE tuples name a constraint class + params directly (keep-out, margin, velocity box, rotation lock) and reuse the existing compiler. The one candidate where the router is the center rather than an appendage.
candidates.failure_safety: Split: fail-safe on the instruction tier when calibrated abstention biases toward refusal/conservative default (over-refusal costs SSR precision, measurable offline). Fails UNSAFE on scene hazards it fails to flag — it has no floor of its own, so it must sit above C1 or C2; root-of-trust isolation also concentrates trust in one model (RoboGuard's acknowledged single point of trust).
candidates.cost_weeks: 1-1.5 weeks: prompting + tuple schema + router glue (router hooks exist in the CAVF plan), offline SSR evaluation is pure CPU/API, conformal gate reuses the same ConU machinery as C2. Cheapest candidate; zero GPU rollout dependency for its headline metric.
candidates.risks: (1) Standalone thinness — an ICRA reviewer can read it as 'prompting + a switch statement' unless the conformal modality gate and the SSR L2 numbers carry it. (2) Dependence on predicate-state quality (garbage predicates in, confident garbage routing out). (3) Over-refusal on benign L2-lookalike scenes tanks the F1 precision term — the twin-scenario structure of HazardArena/SSR punishes exactly this. (4) Monthly API spend limit constrains which VLM can play governor; local Qwen may be below the competence regime the calibration survey warns about.
candidates.benchmark_fit: LIBERO-Safety SSR is the marquee fit: refusal-F1 against published 0.31-0.46 (L2 20-36%), evaluable OFFLINE on released image+instruction pairs before any integration. HazardArena twin scenarios as secondary. SafeLIBERO: only the router tier. OopsieVerse: modality routing for damage-prone requests.

verdict:
Ranking under explicit uncertainty: (1) C2 FOL-COMPILE v2, p(right headline) ~0.40 — it is the direct generalization of our only 100%-validated identification result, most code exists, it alone covers all five hazard classes, and it owns three named white-spaces (runtime rule authorship, calibrated semantic predicates, heterogeneous compilation contract). Its weakness is error direction: it fails unsafe like every enumerator. (2) C1 SANCTION, p ~0.35 — the strongest novelty and the only structurally fail-safe design; both surveys independently declare its gap unclaimed, and it uniquely covers unnamed/dynamic hazards (LIBERO-Safety's intruding hand for free). Its risk is the corridor-liveness failure that demonstrably killed v18, mitigated but not yet proven by in-denoising re-planning. (3) C4 GOVERNOR — adopt as the router tier almost regardless of ranking (1-1.5 weeks, offline-evaluable, targets the SSR L2 gap where published best is 20-36%), but it cannot headline alone. (4) C3 GRAD-RISK — demote to a mechanism inside C2's margin/velocity classes; its novelty does not survive 2512.08233.

The honest strategic read: C1 and C2 are not exclusive — the likely paper is a layered stack (C1 occupancy floor that fails safe, C2 semantic typing that adds heterogeneous classes and exemption sanctioning, C4 router on top), which is itself the survey's 'unified identification stack' gap. The protocol below decides which layer is the headline claim.

Comparison protocol (Weeks 1-2, mostly offline): E1 — extend the 21-scene benchmark to ~150-200 labeled scenes from the 400 saved episodes; measure C1 exemption precision/recall, C2 predicate/hazard F1, C4 route accuracy, and conformal set sizes at alpha=0.05/0.1 (days, no GPU). E2 — corridor-clearance precompute: at calibrated occupancy inflation, does a collision-free corridor to the target survive on each saved episode? This predicts C1's TSR ceiling before any rollout; gate: >=70% clearance or C1 demotes to floor-only. E3 — identification-swap smokes: hold Tier-GT DCBF guidance fixed, swap only the identification source (GT / C1 / C2 / C1+C2) on Spatial L1+L2, n=10/task (~2-3 GPU days); this attributes TSR/CAR deltas purely to identification, our core thesis. E4 — offline SSR refusal-F1: C4 governor vs C2 instruction-rules vs direct-VLM baseline on released LIBERO-Safety pairs; gate: F1 > 0.5 makes SSR a co-headline. E5 — fail-safety stress test: inject identification errors (corrupted detections, flipped votes, dropped rules) and measure error DIRECTION (CAR vs TSR movement) per candidate — this quantifies the fail-safe claim and is itself a publishable figure no surveyed paper has. Decision: E3 is the arbiter; E2 and E4 are the cheap early gates; if E2 fails, C2-headline + C1-as-conservative-fallback-mode; if E2 passes and E5 shows the asymmetry, C1's fail-safe framing leads.
